why_a_successor_exists.defect: In v1, arm B (REIMPLEMENTATION_CONTROL_ARM for MEC-GREEDY_ACCEPT_ON_HELD_OUT_SCALAR) used a running-max incumbent over an i.i.d. candidate stream. That is a monotone ratchet: measured acceptance rate collapsed to 0.014, so arm B accepted almost nothing and its rates were not comparable to any other arm.
why_a_successor_exists.classification: CONFORMANCE_REPAIR_TO_THE_FROZEN_SPEC, not a threshold rescue. v1's own arms[B].steelman_spec already required a steelman control; the v1 implementation did not realize it. No success threshold, no gate, no QoI definition and no falsifier is weakened here.
why_a_successor_exists.chronology_disclosure: v1 results WERE seen before this successor was frozen. Therefore: arms A, C and D are byte-identical to v1 and retain their pre-result freeze. Arm B in v1.1 is a post-result repaired control and is labelled as such. Any v1.1 claim that depends on arm B is weaker in chronology than a claim depending only on A/C/D.
why_a_successor_exists.v1_retained: research/paper6_scoped_utility_v1/RESULTS_V1.json is preserved unmodified as negative process history and is not reinterpreted.

changes_from_v1: Arm B acceptance rule replaced: accept iff best-of-k held-out scalar exceeds a threshold tau.

tau is calibrated on a DISJOINT calibration split (not the evaluation split) so that arm B's acceptance rate matches arm D's acceptance rate at the same n_repro. This makes A/B/D comparable at MATCHED THROUGHPUT rather than at an arbitrary operating point.
Population, seeds, gate contract, numeric contract, availability anchor: unchanged.

scalar_informativeness_model.primary: NEUTRAL - the held-out scalar is drawn independently of ground-truth soundness. Chosen because it is the conservative option: it does not author an advantage for the governed arms.
scalar_informativeness_model.sensitivity_not_headline: LEAKAGE_INFLATED - unsound candidates draw higher held-out scalars, modelling the fact that leakage/threshold-rescue defects inflate exactly the metric an ungoverned scalar rule reads. More realistic, but it stacks the comparison against arm B, so it is reported as a clearly-labelled sensitivity variant and may not carry a headline.
scalar_informativeness_model.rule: Any reported governance benefit must hold under the NEUTRAL model. The sensitivity variant may only strengthen an already-supported statement, never create one.

matched_throughput_contract.definition: At each n_repro, arm B's tau is set so acceptance_rate(B) ~= acceptance_rate(D) on the calibration split.
matched_throughput_contract.why_D_is_the_reference: D executes the identical gate contract on the identical observations and differs from A only in the fail-closed rule. It is therefore the highest-throughput GOVERNED operating point, and matching B to it isolates 'what does reading the gates buy at equal throughput'.

additional_falsifier: F5: If, at matched throughput and under the NEUTRAL scalar model, arm D's false_promotion_rate is not below arm B's, then executing the gate contract buys nothing at equal throughput and the only remaining governance claim is the fail-closed one.
